doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

chapter: Jazz players and the record industry
title: Streaming and the flood of new records
summary: Gold doesn't care about delivery formats, finds streaming pay confusing, and notes the thousands of records released daily.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Well the reason I brought it up is I asked him, now this goes back a number of years, but I asked him, because he worked for Atlantic and then he had his own labels. And we were taking about the different delivery system now, from LPs to where things are at now and if it mattered to him. And he goes, "Naa I don't care. I just make the product and whatever they do with it —" so do you care?

I don't care but in one way I'm not — I don't understand it a lot anymore. You know? I mean I have a subscription for Apple Music. So if I want to hear a song I put the name of the song in, I can hear it. Okay. So I guess that's how people make their living, you know? Through usage. But people are always complaining that they don't get paid enough from Spotify and they don't get paid enough for this or that or that or this. So it's a little confusing.
Yeah. Well I'm going to wrap up —

Also the fact that there's so many home studios and everyone who makes a record they are like I don't know, I think, you can look this up, I might be wrong but there are thousands and thousands of records released every day. That was not the case when John and I grew up.
Yeah. It's a little less special.
